standard_prerequisites.name: If A is pseudo-coherent as a module over R[x] then after the flat base change R[x] -> R[x, y] the algebra A[y] = A \otimes_{R[x]} R[x, y] is pseudo-coherent over R[x, y]
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the composed surjection a pseudo-coherent presentation.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a surjection A' -> B' of rings with B' pseudo-coherent as an A'-module, m-pseudo-coherence (resp. pseudo-coherence) of a complex of B'-modules over B' is equivalent to m-pseudo-coherence (resp. pseudo-coherence) over A'
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the composed presentation into the stated equivalence.

core_obligations: Choose surjections R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and A[y_1, ..., y_m] -> B; their composition gives a surjection R[x, y] -> A[y] = A \otimes_R[x] R[x, y], which is a flat base change of R[x] -> A, hence A[y] is pseudo-coherent over R[x, y] by the flat-base-change lemma applied to the pseudo-coherent R[x]-module A (proof lines 21652-21662). Since B is a quotient of A[y] and A[y] is pseudo-coherent over R[x, y], the finite-push lemma applied to the surjection R[x, y] -> B gives that K is m-pseudo-coherent over B iff over R[x, y], and over A iff over A[y]; combining the two equivalences with the chain B -> A[y] -> R[x, y] and B -> A -> R[x] yields (1) iff (2) (proof lines 21663-21665).
proof_roadmap: Build the composed presentation R[x, y] -> A[y] -> B and transfer pseudo-coherence of A across the flat base change (proof lines 21652-21662).
Apply the finite-push lemma twice along the chain of surjections to get the equivalence (proof lines 21663-21665).
